judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence refers to a Company 'designated by an X in the box below' but the certificate shows only a single name with no visible box or mark, a minor mechanical gap rather than a real ambiguity of meaning. The identity of the insurer (Zurich American) is nonetheless plain on the face of the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the certificate names a different insurer; the closing issuance paragraph refers to 'the Company' and the Master Policy consistently. No conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The claims-made-and-reported trigger — 'made and reported in writing to the Company during the "Certificate Period" or any applicable extended reporting period' — turns on the undefined phrase 'applicable extended reporting period' and on what counts as a 'Claim' first made, terms that insureds and insurers routinely read differently. It also uses a comma splice before 'DEFENSE COSTS', but that does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Item 5's 'Certificate Period', which on this face is garbled/illegible, and on the Master Policy's definitions imported by the issuance paragraph and Items 7-8, so the reporting window cannot be fixed from the certificate alone. That dependency is a genuine, if unresolved, source of whole-instrument friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure identification entry naming one individual and an address; the only defect is an OCR-level typo ('lrem') that changes nothing substantive. There is no term capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is cross-referenced by Item 5 ('address shown in Item I') and by Item 4's per-'Named Certificate Holder' limits, and is consistent with both. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The additional-insured entry is a run-on list — 'Protective Life Insurance Company and Empire General and the Registered Representatives of ProEquities, [Inc.]' — whose scope is genuinely uncertain: whether 'Registered Representatives' means all such representatives or only this holder, and whether 'Empire General' is a separate entity, are questions the words do not settle. judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Item 6, which distinguishes claims 'involving products of Protective Life and ProEquities, Inc.' from 'all other covered products', and against Item 1's single named holder, so the persons and products covered are defined by two different lists that do not obviously match. That mismatch is the most plausible construction fight in this one-page instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-tier deductible turns on 'covered claims involving products of Protective Life and ProEquities, Inc.' versus 'all other covered products', and neither 'covered products' nor 'involving' is defined in the certificate, leaving a specific-list-plus-catch-all structure whose reach is contestable. Whether a sale of an outside or unapproved product falls in the second tier — and is thereby conceded to be covered — is exactly the sort of argument the words invite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Item 2's additional insureds (the same two entities) and with the Master Policy incorporated by the issuance paragraph, the certificate's assumption that 'all other covered products' exist may or may not match the Master Policy's coverage grant, which is where an incoherence would appear. That relationship is the strongest Category 2 candidate here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Refer to Master Policy' is a bare cross-reference with no ambiguous term of its own; it states no amount and creates nothing to construe within itself. Its brevity is a delegation, not a defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Again a pure referral; the only softness is that the endorsements effective at inception are unidentified, so what modifies coverage cannot be read off this document. That is incompleteness rather than a nameable lexical ambiguity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It both incorporates the Master Policy ('issued in accordance with') and declares that 'this policy embodies all agreements existing between the Named Certificate Holder and the Company', while sweeping in 'the application and any attachments hereto' as the holder's representations — 'this policy' is undefined as between certificate and master policy, and the sentence is truncated mid-clause ('RELATING TO THIS'). The truncation and the 'GR' for 'OR' are mechanical errors in the operative merger language.
